correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the coset condition to determinant one and a trace equation. For nonzero trace of x, the SL2 identity h+h^{-1}=(tr h)I forces every h to be an involution; the resulting elementary abelian subgroup lies in one unipotent root group of order q. For trace zero, the group-span algebra A is trace-orthogonal to invertible x. Nondegeneracy of the trace pairing excludes dimension four, and a direct one-dimensional-orthogonal-complement argument excludes dimension three, so A is commutative of dimension at most two. The three quadratic-algebra types give determinant-one groups of orders q-1, q, q+1. The Frobenius/norm-one construction attains q+1. Exhaustive q=2,4 checks agree with every bound; those checks are supplementary rather than an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating all-field theorem has a vacuous finite-group conclusion after specialization to a finite field, whereas this result extracts exact group structure and a sharp extremal order in the first nontrivial matrix dimension. Characteristic two is structurally distinctive: the extremal value is q+1 and is controlled by the nonsplit norm-one torus, while nonzero trace forces a unipotent subgroup of size at most q. This is a natural boundary theorem rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
